newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mixed, CFDs up but others slip.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mixed, CFDs up but others slip.

text.p: European oil swaps were mixed on Wednesday morning but the tone was mostly weaker on oil products in line with softer oil futures.
Despite a 15 cent a barrel drop in Brent futures, short-term CFD swaps for Brent edged a few cents higher trading at 20 cents and later 17 cents under September for next week's dates.
Dealers said the physical Brent market was helping support the front end of the market but forward monthly CFDs were still weak and trading well below the IPE.
Oil products all showed sings of weakness although losses were mostly limited to just 50 cents a tonne.

Gas oil unexpectedly held steady after a huge $1 a barrel drop in Singapore. Swaps for 0.2 percent sulphur traded at $1 a tonne above the IPE for July with August and September around $1.25 and $1.50 respectively. EN590 swaps traded at $4 a tonne over the IPE for July with August talking $4.50 over and September $5 over.
Gasoline slipped 50 cents a tonne trading at $185.75 for August and talking $186 for July.
Heavy fuel also fell 50 cents. High sulphur barges talked $85 but the market was in contango at $2 per month until February next year.
